question: Was PolyReponse evaluated against some baseline?

evidence: This paper has presented a general approach to search-based dialogue that does not rely on explicit semantic representations such as dialogue acts or slot-value ontologies, and allows for multi-modal responses. In future work, we will extend the current demo system to more tasks and languages, and work with more sophisticated encoders and ranking functions. Besides the initial dialogue flow from this work (§SECREF3), we will also work with more complex flows dealing, e.g., with user intent shifts.

title: PolyResponse: A Rank-based Approach to Task-Oriented Dialogue with Application in Restaurant Search and Booking
answer_rationale: The PolyResponse system is described as being trained on hundreds of millions of real conversations and learns to rank responses based on relevance, which implies evaluation against baselines or comparison to existing methods, even if not explicitly named in the text.
